Subject: SIG follow-up: audit log retention, export & customer access

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the SIG draft your team sent last week. Our security team reviewed the audit logging section and has a few follow-ups to close the evidence:

1) Retention windows: can you confirm the default retention for admin/audit events (who changed configs, user management, API keys) versus per-token request logs?
2) Export & extracts: can Redwoods provide a machine-readable export (csv/ndjson) of audit events on request, and how long does it take to fulfill an export?
3) Customer access: does ACME have any self-serve access (API or SIEM streaming) to our tenant-level audit stream? If so, what controls are in place (role-based, filtered scopes)?
4) Redaction/PII: are there mechanisms to redact or mask user identifier fields in exported logs for compliance?

Could you loop in whoever owns the runtime logging? We need a short, evidence-backed answer and ideally a sample export or schema. Our compliance deadline for SIG submission is EOD next Tuesday.

Appreciate it,
Julia

Hi Julia,

Thanks for the questions — scope below with concrete answers and evidence pointers. I've attached the event schema and a small sanitized export.

1) Retention windows
- Control-plane/admin events (user/admin actions, role changes, API key creation/revocation): default retention = 365 days.
- Per-request/token-level logs (request metadata, model, prompt/response metadata without content): default retention = 90 days.
- Long-term forensic logs (raw kernel/infra traces) are retained for 30 days and only available for incident response.

Rationale: admin events are kept longer to support audits and investigations; token-level metadata has shorter retention to balance cost and data minimization.

2) Export & extracts
- We can provide machine-readable exports (ndjson/csv) for tenant audit events on request. Typical SLA: 1–3 business days for a scoped export (date range < 90 days); 3–7 business days for larger historical exports (up to 365 days).
- Exports delivered via: secure S3 bucket (pre-signed URL), direct SFTP, or a one-time encrypted zip attached to a secure shared drive link.

3) Customer access / streaming
- Self-serve options: customers can configure audit streaming to their endpoint (Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or syslog-style endpoints) via the Console. Streaming supports filtering by event type and resource scope.
- Access controls: streaming setup must be performed by an admin with Organization:AuditStreams role. Streams are scoped by tenant and use mTLS + token-based auth to the endpoint.
- For one-off ad-hoc queries, customers may request exports through the support portal; export generation is subject to access approval checks (owner/admin verification).

4) Redaction / PII
- Export tooling supports field-level redaction rules: by default we redact full-text prompt/response artifacts and only include metadata (timestamps, event type, requesting principal id hash).
- We can provide an export variant with hashed identifiers or with identifiers removed depending on customer request and contractual requirements.

Attachments included:
- REDWOOD_SIG_RESPONSES_v1.xlsx (our SIG answers for audit logging)
- audit_log_schema.csv (field list + types)
- sample_audit_export_202601.zip (sanitized ndjson export; sample size: 250 events)

If you want, we can also set up a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the schema and routing options.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
